summary: A group of young hackers meets in a tent-lined space that blocks radio and cell signals, a portable security setup being demoed at a security conference. The narrator, Zenobia ("Zen"), bristles at teasing from Zeke, Jason (called Gargle), and Ian, who are discussing her brother's situation: an informant was recruited in an FBI sting, the agent running it has been identified, and one suspect remains on the run and has been texting her. The conversation shifts to software updates and surveillance, and Jason asks how much the fugitive knows about surveillance.
one_line: Zenobia and a group of hackers meet in a signal-blocking tent to discuss her brother's FBI sting and a fugitive still on the run.
key_facts: The narrator's full name is Zenobia, and she says she can be called Zen for short.
Zenobia is described as a badass woman warrior who led a rebellion against the Romans and conquered Egypt.
Jason, whom the narrator knew as Gargle, says a friend recently bought the place and plans to convert it into a community makerspace.
The tent fabric blocks radio waves and cell signals and is portable security for sensitive communications.
Jason says the tent is being demoed at the security conference.
The narrator made her backpack into a Faraday cage using layers of duct tape and foil.
Ian says the group has identified the crook who was recruited as an informant.
Ian says the group uncovered the FBI agent running the sting and found nothing embarrassing in his past, except a tenth grade yearbook photo that Zeke calls embarrassing.
Ian says one person is still on the run.
The fugitive, nicknamed Wheeze, has sent the narrator a few texts.
The narrator and the fugitive are both running Convo, a messaging app that Zeke says is his.
Zeke warns of a kernel problem in the latest update that reportedly bricked some devices.
The narrator says she is running current versions and calls Zeke's warning redundant.
Ian jokes that the narrator was raised by wolves, and the narrator replies she was raised in Brookline by totally normal people.
Jason asks how much the fugitive knows about surveillance, and the narrator says he is pretty informed.
